newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian watchdog to examine ENEL move.
newsitem.headline: Italian watchdog to examine ENEL move.

text.p: The Italian energy sector watchdog said on Thursday it intended to examine a decision by electricity utility ENEL to stop buying excess power supplies from independent producers and municipal companies.
The watchdog said in a statement it would assess the technical and economic consequences of the decision for the national electricity service, as well as effects on tariffs.
It would also look into the significance of ENEL's move for the various producers and distributors of the public service.
It had recommended ENEL should avoid initiatives that might harm the environment and efficient use of resources.
Earlier, financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported that the energy utility was set to stop buying excess electricity supplies from the private sector. No comment was available from ENEL.
Il Sole said the value of the excess production was about 500 billion lire ($280 million) per year for ENEL and that the move followed talks between ENEL and the energy authority.
The move would benefit ENEL's balance sheet, the paper added.

It would not affect private electricity plants which are dedicated to producing electricity for ENEL. But private groups such as Edison and Sondel, part of the Falck group, will be effected as they sell their excess electricity supplies to ENEL.
These two private groups account for around 70 percent of this type of excess electricity sold to ENEL, Il Sole said.
